title: Bank Card Dispute Guide
excerpt: Confirm whether the card is in the customer's possession, review the transaction, block the card when necessary, and create a dispute.

title: Card Lock Guide
excerpt: Locking a card helps prevent new card authorizations when suspicious activity is suspected. It does not guarantee that already-authorized pending transactions will stop; an existing pending transaction may still post or may drop off. Locking the card and disputing a completed unauthorized charge address different risks and can both be appropriate.

title: Provisional Credit Guide
excerpt: Some card disputes may qualify for provisional credit after the dispute case is opened and reviewed.

title: Transaction Status Guide
excerpt: A completed transaction has posted to the account and can be reviewed for dispute when unauthorized. A pending transaction has been authorized but has not posted; it may post or drop off, and locking the card does not guarantee it will stop. A declined transaction did not post. When suspicious activity exists, locking the card helps prevent new authorizations while completed unauthorized transactions should be reviewed for dispute.
